items.title: The Boxes That Looked the Same

A.question: What is the main lesson of the passage?
A.answer: A clear system people can understand by themselves can reduce mistakes without requiring constant help.
A.evidence: A system that people could understand by themselves reduced the need for constant explanation.
A.evidenceJp: 人が自分で理解できる仕組みにすると、いつも説明する必要が減ったのです。
A.reason: The final sentence states the broader lesson from the box redesign.

A.question: Why did the students add large colored cards and example books?
A.answer: To make the three similar-looking boxes easy to tell apart without keeping a helper beside them all day.
A.evidence: All three boxes were brown and had small labels on top. At the end of the first day, many books were in the wrong boxes. Volunteers considered asking one person to stand beside them all day. Instead, students tested a simpler change.
A.evidenceJp: 三つとも茶色で、小さな表示が上についていました。初日の終わりには、多くの本が間違った箱に入っていました。ボランティアは一人が一日中箱のそばに立つことを考えました。その代わり、生徒たちはもっと簡単な変更を試しました。
A.reason: The visual changes directly addressed confusion among nearly identical boxes.

A.question: Which statement is true according to the passage?
A.answer: Each box received a large colored card on the front and an example book near its label.
A.evidence: They added large colored cards to the front of each box and placed one example book beside every label.
A.evidenceJp: 各箱の正面に大きな色付きカードを付け、表示のそばに見本の本を一冊置きました。
A.reason: Both parts of the visual solution are directly stated.

A.question: Why did sorting errors fall even when no helper was nearby?
A.answer: The boxes themselves now gave enough visual information for volunteers to choose the correct category.
A.evidence: The next collection day, sorting errors dropped sharply even when no helper stood nearby.
A.evidenceJp: 次の回収日には、近くに案内する人がいなくても分類ミスが大きく減りました。
A.reason: The result shows that people could use the redesigned labels without continuous explanation.

A.question: What were the three book categories?
A.answer: Children's books, adults' books, and books needing a check.
A.evidence: It had three boxes: books for children, books for adults, and books needing a check.
A.evidenceJp: 箱は子ども向け、大人向け、確認が必要な本の三つでした。
A.reason: The three categories are listed at the beginning.

B.question: In “stand beside them all day,” what does “them” refer to?
B.evidence: Volunteers considered asking one person to stand beside them all day.
B.evidenceJp: ボランティアは一人が一日中箱のそばに立つことを考えました。
B.reason: The nearby plural objects are the three boxes.

B.question: Complete the summary: Instead of adding a full-time helper, the group made the boxes easier to recognize with large colors and ____.
B.evidence: They added large colored cards to the front of each box and placed one example book beside every label.
B.evidenceJp: 各箱の正面に大きな色付きカードを付け、表示のそばに見本の本を一冊置きました。
B.reason: The example books supplied an additional concrete clue for each category.

B.question: Complete the idea: On the next collection day, sorting errors ____.
B.evidence: The next collection day, sorting errors dropped sharply even when no helper stood nearby.
B.evidenceJp: 次の回収日には、近くに案内する人がいなくても分類ミスが大きく減りました。
B.reason: The phrase states the outcome of the visual redesign.

B.question: Where would this sentence fit best: “The group therefore tried to put the explanation into the boxes themselves.”
B.answer: After the sentence saying students tested a simpler change.
B.evidence: Instead, students tested a simpler change. They added large colored cards to the front of each box and placed one example book beside every label.
B.evidenceJp: その代わり、生徒たちはもっと簡単な変更を試しました。各箱の正面に大きな色付きカードを付け、表示のそばに見本の本を一冊置きました。
B.reason: The sentence introduces the idea behind the visual changes that follow.

B.question: What would most likely make the old problem return?
B.answer: Making the boxes look similar again with only small, hard-to-see labels.
B.evidence: All three boxes were brown and had small labels on top. At the end of the first day, many books were in the wrong boxes.
B.evidenceJp: 三つとも茶色で、小さな表示が上についていました。初日の終わりには、多くの本が間違った箱に入っていました。
B.reason: The original similarity and weak labeling were associated with sorting mistakes.
